Marathon Petroleum climbed 0.95% today, posting its strongest close in the six-day period shown. The gain came as oil prices stabilized after recent weakness—US crude held at $96.16 per barrel, with refineries running at a healthy 92.5% capacity utilization. The bounce follows two days of losses, suggesting investor relief that the sharp pullback from late September may have steadied.

The broader backdrop remains mixed for refiners. While Saudi Arabia's pipeline restoration toward the Red Sea is easing supply concerns and crude exports are recovering to prewar levels through the Strait of Hormuz, fuel inventories (gasoline and diesel) remain elevated, which can pressure refining margins. The geopolitical noise around Iran sanctions also adds uncertainty—refiners benefit when oil supply tightens, but any negotiated easing of tensions could keep crude prices in check.
